title: One event, two ways: object-focus -in verbs
objectives: Understand what the Tagalog focus system does
Say the same event with actor focus (kumain ako ng...) and object focus (kinain ko ang...)
Form the three aspects of -in verbs: kinain, kinakain, kakainin
Choose object focus when the object is specific or definite

grammar.title: What 'focus' means: the same event, two ways
grammar.explanation:
In A1 every verb sentence you built put the doer in the ang-slot: 'Kumain ako ng mansanas' — I ate an apple. That is called ACTOR FOCUS: the ang-phrase (ako) is the actor.

Tagalog can describe the exact same event with the roles re-marked. Compare:

Kumain ako ng mansanas. (actor focus) — I ate an apple.
Kinain ko ang mansanas. (object focus) — I ate the apple.

Same eater, same apple, same eating. What changed is which participant sits in the ang-slot. In the second sentence the OBJECT (ang mansanas) is focused, so the actor drops to its ng-form (ko). The verb changes shape to signal this: kumain (actor focus) vs kinain (object focus).

This is the single most important idea in Tagalog grammar: the markers do not mean subject and object the way English word order does. Ang marks whichever participant the verb's affix points to; everyone else takes ng or sa. Learn to see 'Kinain ko ang mansanas' not as backwards, but as spotlighting the apple.

examples.en: Ana read the book. (object focus — same event)
I drank the coffee. (object focus — same event)

grammar.title: Forming -in verbs in the three aspects
grammar.explanation:
Object-focus verbs in this unit use the suffix -in. The citation (dictionary/contemplated-like) form is root + -in: kain + in = kainin, basa + hin = basahin (roots ending in a vowel add h). But in the completed and incompleted aspects, -in disappears and the infix -in- appears near the front instead:

Completed: kinain (ate), binasa (read), ininom (drank), niluto (cooked — roots starting in l use ni- instead of -in-).
Incompleted: repeat the first syllable of the root inside: kinakain, binabasa, iniinom, niluluto.
Contemplated: repeat the first syllable and keep -in: kakainin, babasahin, iinumin, lulutuin.

Notice inumin and lutuin: the root vowel changes (inom to inum-, luto to lutu-) before -in. Gawin (do/make) is slightly irregular: ginawa, ginagawa, gagawin — no -in in the first two.

The actor in these sentences always takes the ng-form: ko, mo, niya, ni Ana. A very common mistake is 'Kinain ako...' — that says the apple ate you! Keep the doer in ng-form: Kinain KO.

examples.tl: Niluto ni Nanay ang adobo kahapon.
Binabasa niya ang balita tuwing umaga.
examples.en: He reads the news every morning.
I will drink/take the medicine later.

examples.tl: Ano ang ginagawa mo? — Ginagawa ko ang proyekto.
examples.en: What are you doing? — I'm doing the project.

grammar.title: When Tagalog speakers prefer object focus
grammar.explanation:
If both versions describe the same event, when do you use which? The core rule: the ang-phrase is understood as SPECIFIC — 'the one we both know about'. So:

Use ACTOR focus when the object is indefinite or unimportant: 'Bumili ako ng saging' — I bought some bananas (any bananas). Also when there is no object at all: 'Kumain na ako.'

Use OBJECT focus when the object is definite or already known: 'Binili ko ang saging' — I bought the bananas (the ones we discussed). Because everyday life is full of specific things — the food on the table, the phone you lost, the homework you were assigned — object focus is extremely common in real speech, often more common than actor focus.

Questions about things also pull toward object focus: 'Ano ang ginawa mo?' (What did you do?), 'Saan mo binili iyan?' (Where did you buy that?). Notice in that last one the actor mo comes before the verb's object — after question words like saan and kailan, the little ng-pronoun jumps forward.

examples.tl: Bumili ako ng tinapay. / Binili ko ang tinapay.
examples.en: I bought some bread. / I bought the bread (the specific bread).

examples.tl: Ano ang kinain mo sa almusal?
examples.en: What did you eat for breakfast?

examples.tl: Nasaan ang cake? — Ay, kinain ko!
examples.en: Where's the cake? — Oops, I ate it!

dialogue.title: Who ate the leftovers?
dialogue.context: Siblings Jopay and Marvin are in the kitchen in the evening. Jopay is looking for the food she left in the fridge.

lines.speaker: Jopay
lines.tl: Marvin, nasaan ang adobo? Hinahanap ko sa ref.
lines.en: Marvin, where's the adobo? I'm looking for it in the fridge.

lines.speaker: Marvin
lines.en: Uh... I ate it earlier. Sorry!

lines.speaker: Jopay
lines.tl: Ano?! Kinain mo ang buong adobo?
lines.en: What?! You ate the whole adobo?

lines.speaker: Marvin
lines.tl: Oo, at ininom ko rin ang juice mo. Gutom na gutom ako pagkagaling sa trabaho.
lines.en: Yes, and I also drank your juice. I was starving after work.

lines.speaker: Jopay
lines.tl: Naku! Ano na ang kakainin ko ngayong gabi?
lines.en: Oh no! What am I going to eat tonight?

lines.speaker: Marvin
lines.tl: Huwag kang magalit. Magluluto ako ng sinigang para sa iyo.
lines.en: Don't be mad. I'll cook sinigang for you.

lines.speaker: Jopay
lines.tl: Talaga? Sige. Lutuin mo na, gutom na ako.
lines.en: Really? Okay. Cook it now, I'm hungry.

lines.speaker: Marvin
lines.tl: Hinahanap ko ang malaking kaldero. Nasaan ba?
lines.en: I'm looking for the big pot. Where is it?

lines.speaker: Jopay
lines.tl: Nasa ilalim ng lababo. Ginamit ko kahapon.
lines.en: Under the sink. I used it yesterday.

lines.speaker: Marvin
lines.tl: Ah, eto. O, hintayin mo lang, mga isang oras.
lines.en: Ah, here it is. Okay, just wait, about an hour.

lines.speaker: Jopay
lines.tl: Sige. Babasahin ko muna ang libro ko sa sala.
lines.en: Okay. I'll read my book in the living room first.

lines.speaker: Marvin
lines.en: I'll call you when it's cooked.

exercises.prompt: 'Kumain ako ng mansanas' and 'Kinain ko ang mansanas' describe...
choices: the same event, with a different participant in the ang-slot
past vs future versions of the event
a polite and an impolite version
exercises.explain: Both mean I ate the apple/an apple. Focus changes which participant ang marks, not what happened.

exercises.prompt: In 'Binasa ni Ana ang libro', which phrase is in the focus (ang) slot?
exercises.explain: Binasa is object focus, so the object (ang libro) takes ang and the actor Ana drops to ni Ana.

exercises.prompt: Kinain ___ ang tinapay. (I ate the bread.)
exercises.hint: In object focus the actor takes the ng-form.
exercises.explain: With an object-focus verb the actor must be in ng-form: ko, not ako. 'Kinain ako' would mean the bread ate me.

exercises.prompt: Which is the completed (past) object-focus form of inumin?
exercises.explain: Ininom is completed (drank). Iniinom is incompleted, iinumin is contemplated, and uminom is the actor-focus verb.

exercises.prompt: ___ ni Nanay ang sinigang kahapon. (Mom cooked the sinigang yesterday.)
exercises.hint: Roots that start with l take ni- in the completed aspect.
exercises.explain: Lutuin has completed form niluto: roots beginning with l (and some others) take ni- instead of the -in- infix.

exercises.prompt: You bought a specific phone you and your friend talked about yesterday. Which sounds most natural?
exercises.explain: A definite, already-known object pulls the sentence into object focus: binili ko ang cellphone = I bought THE phone.

exercises.prompt: Ano ang ___ mo kahapon? (What did you do yesterday?)
exercises.explain: Gawin is irregular: its completed form is ginawa. Questions about things (ano) typically use object focus.

exercises.tl: Kinain ng aso ang hapunan ko.
choices: I fed the dog its dinner.
The dog will eat my dinner.
exercises.explain: Kinain is object focus: ang hapunan ko (my dinner) is what got eaten, and ng aso is the eater.

exercises.prompt: Turn this actor-focus sentence into object focus: 'Bumasa si Miguel ng nobela.' (the specific novel)
exercises.explain: Switching to object focus, the actor drops from si to ni (ni Miguel) and the object rises from ng to ang (ang nobela).

exercises.prompt: I will finish the project tomorrow.
exercises.explain: A definite object (the project) takes object focus: contemplated tatapusin, actor in ng-form ko, object with ang.

exercises.prompt: Hinihintay ka ni Ana sa labas.
exercises.answer: Ana is waiting for you outside.
accept: Ana is waiting for you outside
Ana is waiting for you out there
exercises.explain: Hintayin means 'wait for someone': the person waited for is the focus (ka), and the waiter takes ni.

exercises.prompt: Saan mo ___ ang sapatos na iyan? (Where did you buy those shoes?)
exercises.explain: After the question word saan, the ng-pronoun mo comes early, then the object-focus completed verb binili.

exercises.answer: Ininom ng aso ang kape ko!
accept: Ininom ng aso ang kape ko
Ininom ang kape ko ng aso
exercises.explain: Object focus fits because it's a specific coffee (mine): ininom (completed), actor ng aso, focused object ang kape ko.

exercises.prompt: Why does 'Kinakain ko ang almusal ko tuwing 7:00' use kinakain rather than kinain?
choices: Because it is a repeated/ongoing action (incompleted aspect)
Because almusal starts with a vowel
exercises.explain: The three aspects work exactly the same in object focus: kinakain (incompleted) covers habitual and ongoing eating, kinain is a finished past event.
